createdFor: Independent atmosphere/cloud-only texture on a world-oriented spherical environment in the actual Scene07 Three.js reconstruction

license.note: This generated image is not the CC0 measured lighting HDRI. It was produced for this project with the authorized built-in image generation tool.

reference.role: Appearance guide for sky cloud size, golden-hour color and tonal relationships only; no source photograph pixels are projected or used as scene texture.

image.pixelModification: None; original generated bytes copied into Scene07 namespace.

prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: independent SKY-ONLY 360 by 180 degree equirectangular environment texture for an actual modeled 3D temple scene. Generate a brand-new photographic sky texture. Landscape 2:1 latitude-longitude map, preferably 3072x1536. It must be suitable for mapping to the INSIDE of a 3D sphere, no perspective horizon curvature, no vignette, no foreground.
Reference image role: only guide the golden-hour cloud appearance and color relationships. Do not reproduce or include ANY of its architecture, trees, foliage, mountains, garden, ground, water, railings, bell or objects. The output contains only atmosphere and clouds.
Composition/calibration: horizon exactly halfway down the map at y=50%. Zenith at top, nadir at bottom. Warmest sunlight center at x=25% and elevation 13 degrees, y=42.8%. There is no hard solar disk. The warm broad glow extends across x=13% to 47%. Throughout the upper hemisphere from y=33% to y=49%, create many distinct irregular small broken stratocumulus clouds with softly shaded lavender-gray interiors and luminous thin honey-gold and pale apricot rims. At 10 to 25 degrees above the horizon, clouds should have convincing 3D rounded volume, feathered edges and small open gaps. Especially at x=29% to 43% and y=37% to 48%, show a richly detailed varied cloud field, not empty haze or a smooth gradient; this sector will be the main scene camera. Thin distant cloud banks near the horizon at y=47% to49.7%. Higher clear-sky gaps are gentle pale powder blue, not deep cobalt. The clouds should look like golden-hour natural photography with restrained contrast, similar to the glow and small broken clouds in the reference, rather than storm drama. Soft pale blue zenith, no huge overpowering central cloud. Lower hemisphere contains only unobtrusive soft warm gray/blue atmospheric haze, no ground. Seamless left and right edges, correct equirectangular polar stretching at top and bottom.
Strict exclusions: buildings, temple, architecture, trees, leaves, plants, silhouettes, mountains, land, ocean, water, sun disc, moons, stars, lightning, people, lens flare, rays drawn across foreground, text, watermark, border. Never make a replacement frame of the complete reference scene.

radiance.interpretation: LDR sRGB texture hardware-decoded to linear, times gain1.3. An artistic camera-sky radiance proxy, distinct from the retained measured CC0 Qwantani HDR illumination.

calibration.coordinateConvention: Longitude atan2(z,x), latitude asin(y), +Y up; PNG top-origin V converted through TextureLoader flipY. Direction = [cos(lat)*cos(lon),sin(lat),cos(lat)*sin(lon)].
calibration.centroidMethod: Display luma L=.2126R+.7152G+.0722B in 8-bit RGB; weights max(0,L-235)^2 within x10..45%,y25..60%; broad luminous rim region, no hard solar disk.
calibration.alignment: Yaw rotates measured source glow longitude onto actual directional light longitude; second rotation about target azimuth tangent aligns glow elevation. Full values retained in native render report info.

status.note: Candidate pending actual native full/detail inspection; no claim of photographic scene match.
